final:
STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: One reproduced violation of criterion 11: a trailer the handler declares and sets after the body is written also appears as a regular response header when ETag is in the chain. The rest of the attack (compression, GetHead, ServeContent, io.Copy/ReadFrom, 1xx, capabilities, panic, concurrency) held up. Probe files are deleted and `git status` matches the starting state.

FILES TOUCHED: none (scratch probes `middleware/zz_probe_test.go` and `middleware/zz_probe2_test.go` were created and removed)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Late declared trailer leaks into headers. Reproduced with `Trailer: X-Sum`, `Write("abc")`, then `Header().Set("X-Sum","zz")`, over httptest.Server. Without ETag: `header.X-Sum=""`, `trailer.X-Sum="zz"`. With `r.Use(ETag)`: `header.X-Sum="zz"`, `trailer.X-Sum="zz"`. Cause: `finish` copies `lateTrailers` back into the header map before `WriteHeader(200)`, so the value goes out as a header too. Criterion 11 says late changes must look the same as without the middleware.
- [minor] `If-None-Match` parsing stops at the first malformed member on a line, so `"a b", "abc"` does not match `"abc"`. Not a stated criterion violation (malformed members never match), so only a note. Not reproduced as a bug.
- [minor] The multi-line `If-None-Match` probe I wrote was wrong (it compared against a literal, not the SHA-256), so it is not a finding.

CHECKS:
- `r.Use(ETag, Compress(5))` over real server, Accept-Encoding gzip → pass (gunzip matches body; gzip ETag ≠ identity ETag; gzip ETag gives 304 with empty body; Vary kept on 200 and 304; Content-Encoding removed on 304; identity ETag gives 200)
- `r.Use(Recoverer, ETag, GetHead)` GET/HEAD over real server → pass (same ETag, HEAD body empty, HEAD with INM → 304); Recoverer panic → 500, no ETag → pass
- `http.ServeContent` (no own ETag, and own `"own"` ETag): 200 with ETag and Last-Modified kept, Range → 206 passthrough with no ETag, own-ETag INM via weak form → 304, HEAD → no body, INM on generated → 304 → pass. Baseline HEAD ServeContent with/without ETag gives identical Content-Length and no ETag → no finding.
- `io.Copy` from `*os.File` (1 MB) and `strings.Reader`, direct `ReadFrom` → pass (body and ETag correct)
- ifNoneMatch table (35 cases: weak both ways, tabs/spaces, empty members, only commas, malformed `abc`/`"abc`/`W/abc`, prefix/superstring, case, `*`, handler-invalid ETag, multi-line) → pass, except the 2 I mis-specified (NUL and space-in-tag), which are not findings
- Non-GET/HEAD (POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, PATCH) with INM → 200, no ETag → pass
- Non-200 (201, 204, 206, 301, 304, 404, 500) with INM `*`: status, headers and body preserved, no ETag → pass; double WriteHeader → first status kept → pass; body before WriteHeader → 200 wins → pass
- 103 Early Hints over raw TCP → 103 first, then 200 with ETag = sha256("final") → pass
- Hijack without Hijacker → "chi/middleware: http.Hijacker is unavailable on the writer"; Push likewise; Unwrap returns the underlying writer → pass
- ResponseController.Flush during buffered 200 over raw TCP → no status line before body completes → pass
- Late ETag and late header after Write → ignored → pass; late header after 201 → not on Result() (same as baseline) → pass
- Panic after WriteHeader+Write → nothing written, panic propagates → pass
- 50 concurrent GET requests through ETag+Compress under `-race` → pass
- HEAD with empty body → no ETag; HEAD handler-set `W/"h"` kept → pass

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should a declared trailer set after the body be sent only as a trailer (matching no-middleware behavior)? The fix is to keep trailer values out of the header map before `WriteHeader`, which means reworking `lateTrailers`.
